text:
anya: starting a canary for Nereid 14b (int4) because we're hitting warm-start OOMs on long generations (>1200 tokens). fragmentation spikes after the first heavy request and stays high.
deploy-bot: Canary launched: nereid-14b-int4 on pool-gamma (12 replicas).
leo: repro steps + environment?
anya: single-client stream, target ~1300 tokens. Observed across A100 and H100 types. microbatch=1 shows it fastest, microbatch=2 sometimes too.
ciara: hypothesis: allocator free-list fragmentation from KV slot allocations during large-attention windows. int4 reduces memory but increases allocation frequency at boundaries. tried similar with other 14b.
ben: quick log excerpt:
```
[E] cudaMalloc failed: OutOfMemory
requested 1.18GiB for attn_kv
allocator state after fail: free_chunks=12, largest_free=64MiB
heap_trend: 2.3GiB -> 1.8GiB -> 420MiB
```
leo: proposed quick mitigations:
- reduce model default max_new_tokens from 1024 -> 512
- disable prefetch on instance startup for warm path
- enable slab_compact_on_eviction
- add startup prime request (~80-120 tokens) to stabilize KV layouts
anya: +1. also suggest a small 20ms batching window with max_concurrent=2 to reduce allocation spikes but keep latency.
ciara: agree. microbatch size stays low for latency; consolidation window handles short bursts.
ben: I'll run A/B overnight comparing baseline vs frag-mit config. Will collect alloc histograms, free-chunk counts, OOM events per replica every 5m and run conv-bench (1k prompts) for quality.
Command I'm using:
```
./canary_runner \
  --model nereid-14b --quant int4 \
  --baseline "max_new=1024,prefetch=true,kv_thresh=0.8,slab_compact=false" \
  --variant  "max_new=512,prefetch=false,kv_thresh=0.6,slab_compact=true,startup_prime=true" \
  --workload long-gen --duration 8h \
  --collect alloc_hist:5m --collect frag_metrics:5m
```
leo: ensure traces for any OOM (stack + alloc site). Also capture latency percentiles and token-rate.
anya: include quality metrics (Rouge/LLMScore) for the variant to rule out regressions from int4+config.
ciara: rollout plan if variant is OK: canary -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24h) -> 100% with auto-fallback to fp16 variant if OOM rate > 0.5%.
ben: running now. will share summary + charts in morning including fragmentation timeline and per-replica OOM counts. :thumbsup:
leo: if tail OOMs persist after this we try kernel affinity for allocator and a small page-align allocator patch. keep infra on-call in the loop for live heap inspection.
anya: reserving 3 spare debug nodes. ping me if you want immediate access.
ben: results posted at 6165518800 (link to plots will be added).
